label: Every approval identity is self-declared and a bot can answer its own item: `--as` is an unauthenticated name, `bots answer` has no caller check, and a BOT.md can declare `sandbox: danger-full-access` with no config cap (OpenCode Bash is also unconfined), so the child can run `bots answer <own-item> yes --as owner`. State the trust boundary and enforce it: tty + per-install operator token for `--as`, cap bot posture at workspace-write unless installed with full access.

The link record names an actor and the roster compares names to names; bind the roster and link to the provider-asserted sender id (Telegram/Slack user id, WhatsApp phone) so the check is about the sender, not a claim.

A linked group chat exposes every approval prompt to its members and only the roster stops a press; state that membership can read and require a direct chat for approval-bearing links or mark group links read-only.
006 states "there is no sign-in to govern" and "no auth" while 011 treats an owner/member roster as a gate; add one shared trust-model paragraph both phases cite.

reason: No actor module exists and 001 CHK-032 confirms the runtime has no sign-in.
repo-config.ts has no sandbox key and posture accepts all three modes.
